question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{1-(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}}\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-{sin}^{2}⁡x}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
